# everpure_azure_snapshots (Data Source)

Lists the Volume Group Snapshots in a Volume Group, including those taken by the volume group's snapshot schedule. Soft-deleted (destroyed, not yet eradicated) snapshots are excluded by default; set `include_destroyed = true` to include them.

The elements do not include `volume_snapshots`, the snapshot of each member volume: the API does not return them when listing. To get them for one snapshot, look it up by name with the [`everpure_azure_snapshot` data source](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/PureStorage-OpenConnect/everpure-azure/latest/docs/data-sources/snapshot).

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    everpure = {
      source = "PureStorage-OpenConnect/everpure-azure"
    }
  }
}

provider "everpure" {
  subscription_id = var.subscription_id
}

variable "subscription_id" {
  type = string
}

data "everpure_azure_volume_group" "example" {
  name            = "vg-prod-east"
  storage_pool_id = "/subscriptions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/resourceGroups/rg-storage-prod/providers/PureStorage.Block/storagePools/pool-prod-east"
}

# Lists the snapshots in the volume group above, including those taken by its
# snapshot schedule. Soft-deleted snapshots are excluded by default.
data "everpure_azure_snapshots" "example" {
  volume_group_id = data.everpure_azure_volume_group.example.id
}

locals {
  # Scheduled snapshot IDs keyed by created_at, an RFC 3339 UTC timestamp, so
  # sorting the keys sorts by time.
  scheduled = {
    for s in data.everpure_azure_snapshots.example.snapshots :
    s.created_at => s.id if s.created_by_policy
  }
}

# Restores vol-prod-data from the most recent scheduled snapshot.
resource "everpure_azure_volume" "restored" {
  name            = "vol-prod-data-restored"
  volume_group_id = data.everpure_azure_volume_group.example.id
  source_type     = "snapshot"

  source_snapshot {
    id          = local.scheduled[reverse(sort(keys(local.scheduled)))[0]]
    volume_name = "vol-prod-data"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `volume_group_id` (String) Full Azure Resource Manager ID of the volume group to list snapshots in. Must be in the provider's own `subscription_id`.

### Optional

- `include_destroyed` (Boolean) Whether to include soft-deleted (destroyed, not yet eradicated) snapshots in the result. Defaults to `false`.
- `limit` (Number) The most snapshots to return: the newest ones, so `limit = 1` returns only the latest. Unset returns every snapshot in the volume group, which in a volume group with many snapshots means many API calls on every read; a read without `limit` that returns more than 1000 snapshots warns.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `snapshots` (Attributes List) The snapshots found, sorted newest first, by `created_at`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--snapshots))

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `read` (String) Defaults to 5 minutes. A duration string: a number with a unit suffix s (seconds), m (minutes) or h (hours); segments can be combined, e.g. "30m" or "1h30m". Used when reading the snapshots.


<a id="nestedatt--snapshots"></a>
### Nested Schema for `snapshots`

Read-Only:

- `created_at` (String) When the snapshot was created, as an RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC. Timestamps sort chronologically as strings.
- `created_by_policy` (Boolean) Whether the snapshot was taken by the volume group's snapshot schedule, rather than manually.
- `id` (String) The full Azure Resource Manager ID of the snapshot.
- `name` (String) Name of the snapshot. A soft-deleted snapshot's name is the timestamped name it was renamed to on deletion; see `soft_deletion.previous_name` for its original name.
- `soft_deletion` (Attributes) Soft-delete state, present only when this snapshot is soft-deleted (destroyed, not yet eradicated). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--snapshots--soft_deletion))
- `space` (Attributes) Space usage, in bytes. Null when the service reports none. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--snapshots--space))
- `volume_group_id` (String) Full Azure Resource Manager ID of the volume group the snapshot belongs to. Same as the data source's own `volume_group_id`.

<a id="nestedatt--snapshots--soft_deletion"></a>
### Nested Schema for `snapshots.soft_deletion`

Read-Only:

- `destroyed_at` (String) When it was destroyed, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.
- `eradication_timestamp` (String) Approximate time at which the object will be eradicated automatically, as an RFC 3339 timestamp. Derived from the remaining retention when read, so it can change by seconds to minutes between reads; do not use it for exact comparisons or as an input to other resources. Use `destroyed_at` as the stable reference.
- `previous_name` (String) The name this snapshot had before it was destroyed.


<a id="nestedatt--snapshots--space"></a>
### Nested Schema for `snapshots.space`

Read-Only:

- `shared_in_bytes` (Number) Space occupied by duplicated data, meaning data shared among different volumes and snapshots as a result of data deduplication, in bytes.
- `snapshots_in_bytes` (Number) Space occupied by data unique to one or more snapshots, in bytes.
- `total_used_in_bytes` (Number) Total space occupied by customer data, in bytes. This is the space being billed for.
- `unique_in_bytes` (Number) Unique space occupied by customer data, in bytes.
